diagnosis: The die-cut white outline is a single hand-drawn enlarged triangle/polygon that does not follow the actual jagged multi-tier tree silhouette — it is far too wide at the top (the polygon flares out from x=276 at y=112 versus the actual tier-1 apex at x=298–342) and at the bottom. Additionally, fairy lights and bead garland beads are placed at coordinates that fall outside the actual tree tier boundaries (e.g. cx=162,cy=642; cx=444,cy=560; cx=432,cy=490; cx=198,cy=446) creating disconnected floating dots. The fix: (1) replace the hand-crafted outline shape with a programmatically generated one that uses feMorphology operator=dilate radius=7 applied to a <use> clone of the entire artwork group, rendered white and placed behind everything — this guarantees the border tracks the real artwork automatically; (2) add a clip-path derived from the union of all tree tier paths plus a small outset so stray decorations outside the foliage are clipped away.
